domain_restrictions: x is a real number so that floor(x) and frac(x) are defined
the hypothesis constrains frac(x) to be at least (n-1)/n and strictly less than 1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1 and every real x with fractional part frac(x) in the interval [ (n-1) / n, 1 ), we have F_n(x) equals H_n minus 1, where F_n(x) is floor(n times x) minus the sum for k from 1 to n of (floor(k times x) divided by k), and H_n is the sum for k from 1 to n of 1 divided by k.
quantifier_order: for all n in integers with n > 1
for all real x such that frac(x) is in the interval [(n-1)/n, 1)

variables.name: n
variables.role: parameter indexing the functions F_n and the harmonic number H_n; also determines the summation limits

variables.name: x
variables.role: input to the floor-based expressions; its fractional part determines the case condition

variables.name: k
variables.role: dummy summation index inside the definitions of F_n(x) and H_n

variables.name: F_n
variables.role: defined quantity: floor(n x) minus a weighted sum of floor(k x)

variables.name: frac
variables.role: fractional part of x defined as x minus floor(x)

variables.domain: rational numbers for each fixed integer n >= 2
variables.name: H_n
variables.role: harmonic number defined by sum of 1 over k from 1 to n

witness_dependencies: none: the conclusion gives a direct equality F_n(x) = H_n - 1 once the condition on frac(x) holds; no existential choices are introduced

statement_nl: Let n be an integer greater than 1, define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k, and define frac(x) = x - floor(x). If frac(x) lies in the interval [(n-1)/n, 1), then F_n(x) = H_n - 1, where H_n = sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k.
